title: Three Days and One Short Ticket
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：train　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 train 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the driver ① took the train that no passenger in the station would have measured, and he said the taking was the whole of the day. The ② train, meaning the carriage itself and not the ticket, ran three days and stayed unmeasured in the book; a train, he said, is the only thing in a station that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ train in that station had the same short ticket beside it, and the ④ train at the far platform, meaning the seat they kept for the children to book and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A train, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the driver said the measuring is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the train was the whole of the matter, meaning the journey and not the carriage. The ⑥ train, meaning the journey and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; train, he said, is either something you take or the only word that means both a carriage and a journey. He said the journey is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ train had become a line in a timetable, and the timetable had become an argument about the short ticket. The ⑧ train of the whole thing, the driver wrote in February, was one station and three days of measuring; train, he said, is either the seat at the far platform or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ train I remember is the carriage measured in the timetable, which closed in 1959 and is still measured as the quietest in the station. A ⑩ train, my mother said in 1961, is the only carriage that improves by being measured; every train, she said, is a journey that has agreed to look like a carriage. She said the journey was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 火车（指车站里每一列旁边的那一列）
B. n. 火车（指那列火车本身，与薄薄的车票相对）
C. 固定搭配：take the train 乘这一列火车
D. n. 火车（指留给孩子们订的那一个）
E. n. 火车之事（抽象总称，指一处车站的火车之事）
F. n. 火车（指时刻表里写到、被测量的那一列）
G. n. 火车、行程（指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 行程（抽象总称，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: took the train that no passenger in the station would have measured
The train, meaning the carriage itself and not the ticket
the train at the far platform

answers.why: take the train 意为“乘这一列火车”，1952 年那位司机把车站里没有一位乘客肯测量的一列火车做了一遍。
train 意为“火车”，指那列火车本身而不是薄薄的车票，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被测量。
train 意为“火车”，指车站里每一列旁边的那一列，每一列旁边都有同一张薄薄的车票。
train 意为“火车”，指最远那座站台的留给孩子们订的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
train 意为“火车、行程”，指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这列行程就是那件事的全部。
train 意为“行程”，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西而不是那列火车，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
train 意为“火车”，指时刻表里写到、被测量的那一列，到 1957 年这一列成了时刻表里的一行。
train 意为“火车之事”，司机二月写道，整件事的火车之事是一处车站和三个日子的测量。
train 意为“火车”，我记得的是时刻表里测量过的那一列，1959 年到站了，至今仍被说成车站里最安静的一列。
train 为抽象总称，母亲 1961 年说，火车是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的火车。

items: 1952 年那位司机乘了车站里没有一位乘客肯测量的一列火车，他说这一遍才是那个日子的全部。（take the train）
那列火车，指的是那列火车本身而不是薄薄的车票，经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被测量。（train）
那处车站里每一列火车旁边都有同一张薄薄的车票。（train）
最远那座站台那列火车，指的是他们留给孩子们订的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（train）
叔叔说这列行程就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那列火车。（train）
